translations.text: Our Father, you who are in the heavens, hallowed be your name. May your kingdom come. May your will be done, as in heaven so also on earth.
Give us today our daily bread. And forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors.
And do not lead us into temptation, but deliver us from evil. Our Father, you who are in the heavens, hallowed be your name.
God's name is always hallowed; but when we say this, we pray that his name may be hallowed in us men through good works. May your kingdom come.
The kingdom of God exists always and everywhere; yet when we say this, we pray that God's kingdom may be in us and that the devil's power may be removed from us.
May your will be done, as in heaven so also on earth. We must always pray to God for this: that his will may be done in the same way on earth among men
as it is done in heaven among the angels, so that men on earth may be able to do his will just as the angels in heaven can.
Give us today our daily bread. All of a man's needs that he has for this present life are included under the name of bread.
Therefore whoever wishes should sing this prayer every day, so that God may help him in his needs every day.
And forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors.
Whoever says this needs to do as he says, because if he does not do as he says, he curses himself more than he asks good for himself:
for whoever is angry with another and then sings this prayer is asking evil for himself. And do not lead us into temptation.
God does not lead anyone into any evil, except that when he abandons a person, that person is at once in temptations;
the words mean this: that he should not abandon us, so that we may not be led into evil.
But deliver us from evil. In these words is included every one of the evils that can harm a person.
Therefore whoever sings this prayer with a pure mind should believe that God will then hear him:
for in it he asks for nothing at all except what God himself commanded us to ask for, and yet all of a man's needs are included in it.
These are the deadly (criminal) sins, by which the devil plunges men into hell. Vices of the flesh: lusts of the body. Impurity: uncleanness.
Fornication: whoredom. Lust: wicked desires. Service of idols: worship of false gods. Sorceries: poisonings. Enmity: hostility.
Contentions: strife. Jealousies: rivalry. Angers: hatreds. Brawls: quarrels. Dissensions: disputes. Sects: conflicts. Envy:
ill-will. Obstinate: self-willed. Murders: manslaughters. Anxious: [?] ("angustenter", apparently anxious or distressed). Drunkenness: drinking. Adulteries: adulteries. Thefts:
thefts. I believe in God the Father almighty, creator of heaven and earth. And in Christ the Saviour, his only Son, our Lord,
who was conceived by the Holy Spirit, born of the Virgin Mary, punished under Pontius Pilate, nailed to the cross, dead and buried.
He descended into hell; on the third day he rose from the dead; he ascended into heaven and sat at the right hand of God the Father almighty; from there he will come to judge the living and the dead.
I believe in the Holy Spirit, the holy catholic Church, the communion of saints, the forgiveness of sins, the resurrection of the flesh, and eternal life.
Amen. Whoever wishes to be saved must, before all things, hold the catholic faith.
Unless each person keeps this faith whole and entire, he will without doubt perish forever.
This is the catholic faith: that we worship one God in Trinity and the Trinity in Unity, neither confusing the persons nor dividing the substance.

For the person of the Father is one, the person of the Son is another, and the person of the Holy Spirit is another. But the Godhead of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit is one, their glory equal, their majesty coeternal.
As the Father is, so is the Son, and so is the Holy Spirit. The Father is uncreated, the Son is uncreated, and the Holy Spirit is also uncreated.
The Father is immeasurable, the Son is immeasurable, the Holy Spirit is immeasurable. The Father is eternal, the Son is eternal, the Holy Spirit is eternal.
And yet they are not three eternals, but one eternal. In the same way they are not three uncreated beings or three immeasurable beings, but one uncreated and one immeasurable.
Likewise the Father is almighty, the Son is almighty, and the Holy Spirit is also almighty. And yet they are not three almighties, but one almighty.
Likewise the Father is God, the Son is God, the Holy Spirit is God. And yet they are not three Gods, but one God.
Likewise the Father is Lord, the Son is Lord, the Holy Spirit is Lord. And yet they are not three Lords, but one Lord.

For just as Christian truth compels us to confess each person individually to be God and Lord, so the true Christian religion forbids or prevents us from saying that there are three Gods or three Lords.
The Father is made by none, neither created nor begotten. The Son is from the Father alone, neither made nor created,
but begotten. The Holy Spirit is from the Father and the Son, neither made nor created nor begotten, but proceeding.
So there is one Father, not three Fathers; one Son, not three Sons; one Holy Spirit, not three Holy Spirits.
And in this Trinity none is before or after, none greater or less, but all three persons are coeternal with one another and coequal, so that in all things,
as has already been said above, the Trinity in Unity and the Unity in Trinity is to be worshipped. Whoever wishes to be saved, therefore, should think or understand this about the Trinity.
But it is also necessary for eternal salvation that each person faithfully believe in the incarnation of our Lord, the Saviour Christ.
For the right faith is that we believe and confess that our Lord, the Saviour Christ, the Son of God, is God and man.
He is God, begotten of the substance or essence of the Father before the ages; and he is man, born in the world of the substance of his mother:
perfect God and perfect man, subsisting of a rational soul and human flesh; equal to the Father as to his Godhead, less than the Father as to his humanity.
Although he is God and man, he is still not two, but Christ is one. And he is one, not by the changing of the Godhead into flesh,
but by the taking up of the manhood into God. He is one, certainly, not by a mixing of the substance, but by the unity of the person.
For just as the rational soul and the body are one man, so God and man are one Christ.

He suffered for our salvation, descended into hell, and rose from the dead. He ascended into heaven and sits at the right hand of God the Father almighty. From there he will come to judge the living and the dead.

At his coming all men must rise again with their bodies, and they will give account of their own deeds. Those who have done good will go into eternal life, and those who have done evil into eternal fire.
This is the catholic faith. Unless each person believes it faithfully and firmly, he cannot be saved.
Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace to men of good will. We praise you.
We bless you, we worship you, we glorify you. We give thanks to you for your great glory.
Lord God, heavenly King, God the Father almighty; Lord, only-begotten Son, Saviour Christ; Lord God, Lamb of God, Son of the Father, who takes away the sin of the world, have mercy on us.
You who take away the sin of the world, receive our prayer. You who sit at the right hand of the Father, have mercy on us. For you alone are holy.
You alone are the Lord, you alone are the Most High, Saviour Christ, with the Holy Spirit, in the glory of God the Father. Amen.
